title: PowerPoint on Mac: reference SharePoint and OneDrive files when creating a presentation with Copilot Agent Mode
summary: The briefing states that no administrator action is required, but the sources do not establish that; it should report that no required action is specified instead. The feature description, roadmap details, and both controls' paths and commands are supported. Another Microsoft guidance page uses a different label for the SharePoint control.

claims.where: What's changing; summary; Scope; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Copilot in PowerPoint recognizes SharePoint and OneDrive file references made by file or document name in a prompt.
claims.quote: Copilot in PowerPoint can now recognize references to files stored in SharePoint and OneDrive when you mention them in your prompt, such as by file or document name.

claims.claim: The example instructions allow a reference by document name and/or document owner.
claims.quote: In your prompt, reference a file saved in SharePoint or OneDrive by the document name and/or owner of the document.

claims.claim: Implicit file references were previously unsupported for files in these locations.
claims.quote: Previously, these implicit file references were not supported for files stored in these locations.

claims.where: What's changing; summary; Why it matters; Risk assessment
claims.claim: Copilot can use the referenced file as context when creating the presentation.
claims.quote: You can naturally reference a relevant file in your prompt, and Copilot can use that file as context when creating your presentation.

claims.claim: Users need not first locate and manually attach the referenced file.
claims.quote: You can bring existing SharePoint and OneDrive content into your presentation workflow more naturally, without first locating the file and manually attaching it.

claims.claim: No administrator setting specific to implicit file references is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint Copilot reference files SharePoint OneDrive document name 555897 default admin setting disable implicit references; Copilot PowerPoint Agent Mode licensing reference files requirements admin controls. claims.claim: No admin action is forced.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot PowerPoint Agent Mode licensing reference files requirements admin controls. Read the roadmap and feature release note; neither states that no administrator action is required.
claims.fix: Replace 'No admin action is forced' with 'Neither the roadmap record nor the feature release note specifies required admin action'. This reports the documentation gap without asserting what rollout requires.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Copilot follows existing user access boundaries rather than granting additional access to referenced content.
claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot presents only data that each individual can access using the same underlying controls for data access used in other Microsoft 365 services.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery limits discovery of selected SharePoint-site content in organization-wide search and Microsoft Copilot responses.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery helps you limit discovery of content from specific SharePoint sites, including recently interacted files, in organization-wide search results and Microsoft Copilot responses while those reviews are taking place.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery is a site-level control.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery is a site-level setting.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery applies only to SharePoint sites and is not supported for OneDrive sites.
claims.quote: You can only apply this feature to SharePoint sites. It's not supported for OneDrive sites.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery changes discoverability, not existing permissions.
claims.quote: No. Restricted Content Discovery affects discoverability, not access permissions. Users who already have access to content can continue to access it.

claims.claim: The SharePoint admin center path is Sites > Active sites > site > Settings > Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote:
In the SharePoint admin center, expand Sites and select Active sites.
Select the site you want to configure.
Open the Settings tab, and then turn Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot on.
claims.fix: Keep the path supported by its cited page. Add: 'Microsoft's Copilot readiness guidance instead labels this setting Restrict content discovery.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/get-ready-copilot-sharepoint-advanced-management#step-3-prevent-accidental-oversharing, which says 'Under Restrict content discovery, select On'.

claims.claim: Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true enables Restricted Content Discovery for a site.
claims.quote:
Enable Restricted Content Discovery for a site
Use PowerShell
Open PowerShell as an administrator and run the following command:
Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true

claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 admin center path for a user's license assignment is Users > Active users > user > Licenses and Apps > Licenses.
claims.quote:
In the admin center, go to the Users > Active users page.
Select the row of the user that you want to assign a license to.
In the right pane, select Licenses and Apps.
Expand the Licenses section, select the boxes for the licenses that you want to assign, then select Save changes.

claims.claim: Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @() assigns a license to the specified user.
claims.quote:
To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell.
Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()
